vocab.cn_example: 该国过于拥挤的监狱

vocab.definition: the process of making things fair after a crime
vocab.example: Mr Justice Ellis
vocab.cn_example: 法官埃利斯先生

vocab.definition: a rule which everyone must follow

vocab.cn_example: 法律关于驾车时血液中含有酒精是如何规定的？

vocab.cn_example: 堕胎在你们国家是否合法？

vocab.definition: a group of people whose job is to stop others from breaking rules and laws

vocab.cn_example: 应该增加警力在这一地区步行巡逻。

vocab.definition: a building where criminals are locked away

vocab.cn_example: 监狱里的条件据说糟透了。

vocab.definition: a person who is locked away in a prison or jail

vocab.cn_example: 犯人们爬上监狱屋顶对监狱里的条件表示抗议。

vocab.definition: to make them suffer in some way

vocab.cn_example: 他确实粗暴对待自己的马。

vocab.definition: the act of punishing someone

vocab.cn_example: 许多人认为无论对什么罪行来说，死刑都过于严厉了。

vocab.definition: a fixed way of behaving that people are told to follow

vocab.cn_example: 她在标题下面画了两条红线。

vocab.definition: a person who takes things without asking or paying

vocab.definition: a lie used to mislead or fool a person

vocab.definition: to do things that are good, bad, sensible etc.

vocab.definition: to make water go through a toilet

vocab.cn_example: 他听到马桶的冲水声。

vocab.definition: a mark made by the pattern of lines at the end of a person’s finger

vocab.definition: a police officer whose job is to discover information about crimes and catch criminals

vocab.cn_example: 他扮演一位满嘴俏皮话的侦探。

vocab.definition: to deal with a particular situation

vocab.cn_example: 她的眼光扫过人们的脸。

vocab.definition: to say that the person did something bad

vocab.cn_example: “不是我的错。”“别担心，我不是在指责你。”

vocab.definition: carrying a weapon
vocab.cn_meaning: 使用武器的，用武力的;带武器的，武装的

vocab.cn_example: 据报道，枪手全副武装，配备了步枪和手枪。

vocab.definition: to capture them for a crime they might have committed

vocab.cn_example: 因海关人员在他的包中发现了毒品，他被捕了。

vocab.definition: a small piece of metal that is fired from a gun

vocab.cn_example: 一颗子弹嵌进了男孩的腿里。

vocab.definition: to do something bad

vocab.cn_example: 也许我们应该把这些想法写在纸上，免得忘记。

vocab.definition: being mean or nasty to others

vocab.cn_example: 他的死是个无情的打击。

vocab.definition: intended or planned; it is not an accident
vocab.cn_meaning: （常指坏事）有意的，故意的，蓄意的

vocab.cn_example: 蓄意攻击／侮辱／说谎

vocab.definition: the emotion we feel when we are scared

vocab.cn_example: 拉基莎担心自己的安全，就坐在里面直到警察到来。

vocab.definition: to make someone feel scared

vocab.definition: to stop someone or something from moving

vocab.definition: having done nothing wrong

vocab.cn_example: 她一脸天真无邪，我很难把她往坏里想。

vocab.definition: the punishment you get for a certain crime

vocab.cn_example: 该法令允许判处长达3年的监禁。

vocab.definition: describes something that could happen

vocab.cn_example: 一些潜在的买主表达了对该公司的兴趣。

vocab.definition: to act like you are something or someone you are not

vocab.cn_example: 我不想妄称自己是该学科的专家。

vocab.definition: the possibility that something dangerous may happen

vocab.cn_example: 这个行业的风险和回报都很高。

vocab.definition: a strong emotion people feel when surprised by something bad

vocab.cn_example: 那些饥饿儿童的照片让人们深感震惊，都纷纷解囊相助。

vocab.definition: to think someone might have done something bad

vocab.cn_example: 没有人知道谁杀了她，但是警方认为她丈夫有嫌疑。

vocab.definition: the feeling you have when you don’t trust someone or something
vocab.example: "I'm arresting you on suspicion of illegally possessing drugs," said the police officer.
vocab.cn_example: 警官说：“你涉嫌非法持有毒品，我将拘捕你。”

vocab.definition: the process that decides whether someone is guilty or innocent
vocab.example: trial proceedings
vocab.cn_example: 审判程序

vocab.definition: a person who sees a crime take place

vocab.cn_example: 警方呼吁那场事故的目击者站出来。

vocab.definition: to quickly follow someone or something in order to catch them

vocab.cn_example: 经过短暂追捕，小偷被警察擒获。

vocab.definition: to have an accident in a car, plane etc by violently hitting something else

vocab.cn_example: 撞车事故

vocab.definition: when you catch someone in order to make them a prisoner

vocab.cn_example: 斯旺森说服了赫布利秘密工作以捕获凶手。

vocab.definition: to take hold of someone or something with a sudden or violent movement

vocab.cn_example: 他猛地伸出手去抓她。

vocab.definition: the crime of stealing money or things from a bank, shop etc.

vocab.cn_example: 我从来不擅长算术。

vocab.definition: a very large number made up of a thousand million

vocab.cn_example: 到处都有许多的苍蝇。

vocab.definition: to work out the amount or number of something using math

vocab.cn_example: 据计算，近期风暴造成的损失超过了500万英镑。

vocab.definition: a tool used in math which allows you to draw a perfect circle
vocab.example: A compass needle points north.
vocab.cn_example: 罗盘指针指向北方。

vocab.definition: to split it into several smaller parts

vocab.cn_example: 讲座结束后，我想让所有学生分成几个讨论小组。

vocab.definition: the act of dividing numbers

vocab.cn_example: 工人间工作的平均分配

vocab.definition: another way of saying twelve

vocab.cn_example: 一打鸡蛋

vocab.cn_example: 电影有把暴力和刺激相等同的倾向。

vocab.cn_example: 6是偶数，7是奇数。

vocab.definition: a mathematical relationship or rule expressed in symbols
vocab.example: He developed a formula for calculating the area of a triangle.
vocab.cn_example: 他发明了计算三角形面积的公式。

vocab.definition: a part of a whole number or thing
vocab.example: ¼ and 0.25 are different ways of representing the same fraction.
vocab.cn_example: 1/4和0.25是同一分数的不同表达方式。

vocab.definition: a picture that shows us numbers or quantities
vocab.cn_meaning: （通常用直线或曲线表示的）图，图表，图解

vocab.cn_example: 这幅图显示出在过去20年里犯罪率与失业率的变化关系。

vocab.definition: smaller in size or value than another

vocab.cn_example: 我们必须尽量少花一些钱。

vocab.definition: the part of a sum that tells us to take something away
vocab.example: Temperatures could fall to minus eight tonight.
vocab.cn_example: 今晚气温会降到零下8度。

vocab.definition: to increase a number by adding that number to itself a certain number of times

vocab.cn_example: 这些生物能迅速大量繁殖。

vocab.definition: a type of number which tells you where something comes in a list
vocab.example: Fifth and 200th are ordinal numbers.
vocab.cn_example: 第五（Fifth）和第二百（200th）都是序数词。

vocab.definition: a number or value compared to a total value of 100

vocab.cn_example: 你20%的答案是对的，也就是说每5个中有1个是对的。

vocab.cn_example: 6加4等于几？

vocab.cn_example: 他把橙子切成了4块。

vocab.definition: a piece of paper that proves you can do a certain thing

vocab.cn_example: 出生／结婚／死亡证明

vocab.definition: the skill which allows people to make or invent things

vocab.cn_example: 太多的规则可能会扼杀创造力。

vocab.definition: an award given to a student when they finish at university

vocab.cn_example: 她获得了爱丁堡大学的物理学学位。

vocab.definition: to think about one thing clearly

vocab.definition: to complete or answer it

vocab.cn_example: 我们备有各种各样的香水。

vocab.definition: used to mean that a fact can easily be noticed or understood

vocab.example: She does not like anyone challenging her authority.
vocab.cn_example: 她不喜欢任何人挑战她的权威。

vocab.definition: extremely
vocab.example: It was incredibly hard work.
vocab.cn_example: 那是个非常艰辛的工作。

vocab.definition: feeling or showing a lot of interest and excitement about something
vocab.example: He is an enthusiastic skier.
vocab.cn_example: 他是个热情的滑雪爱好者。

vocab.definition: to show that an event or occasion is important by doing something special
vocab.example: I was in a mood to celebrate.
vocab.cn_example: 我很想庆祝一番。

vocab.definition: to make them slightly angry
vocab.example: Tina really annoyed me in the meeting this morning.
vocab.cn_example: 在今天上午的会上，蒂娜真是把我气坏了。

vocab.definition: the feeling that something is true or real
vocab.example: His belief in God gave him hope during difficult times.
vocab.cn_example: 他对上帝的信奉使他在困境中看到了希望。

vocab.definition: to be a part of something
vocab.example: After three years in Cambridge, I finally feel as if I belong here.
vocab.cn_example: 在剑桥呆了3年以后，我终于找到了归属感。

vocab.definition: the ability to make others like you
vocab.example: a woman of great charm
vocab.cn_example: 魅力十足的女人

vocab.definition: to behave in a dishonest way in order to get what you want
vocab.example: Anyone caught cheating will be immediately disqualified from the exam.
vocab.cn_example: 任何人如被发现作弊将被立即取消考试资格。

vocab.definition: being extremely sad
vocab.example: In a depressed market, it's difficult to sell goods unless you lower your prices.
vocab.cn_example: 市场不景气只能降价，否则很难把产品卖出去。

vocab.definition: to upset someone by not doing what they expected
vocab.example: I'm sorry to disappoint you, but I'm afraid I can't come after all.
vocab.cn_example: 很抱歉让你失望，但恐怕我真的来不了。

vocab.definition: feeling like a fool in front of others
vocab.example: She felt embarrassed about undressing in front of the doctor.
vocab.cn_example: 在医生面前脱衣服让她觉得很尴尬。

vocab.definition: someone who is clever
vocab.cn_meaning: 有才智的;聪颖的，理解力强的
vocab.example: She's formidably intelligent.
vocab.cn_example: 她聪明绝顶。

vocab.definition: when they wish they had what someone else has
vocab.example: He had always been very jealous of his brother's good looks.
vocab.cn_example: 他兄弟的外貌总是让他嫉妒。

vocab.definition: full of energy and enthusiasm
vocab.cn_meaning: 精力充沛的;生气勃勃的;活跃的
vocab.example: It's hard work teaching a class of lively children.
vocab.cn_example: 给一班活泼好动的孩子们当老师很辛苦。

vocab.definition: feeling sad because they are alone
vocab.example: She gets lonely now that all the kids have left home.
vocab.cn_example: 现在孩子们都离开了家，她感到有些孤独。

vocab.definition: feeling very sad or grumpy
vocab.example: She's miserable living on her own.
vocab.cn_example: 她独自生活，非常可怜。

vocab.definition: describes a bad feeling, reaction, or response
vocab.example: He always looks for the negatives in any situation.
vocab.cn_example: 不管在什么情形下，他总是会找不好的一面。

vocab.definition: feeling worried about something in the future
vocab.example: He suffers from a nervous disorder.
vocab.cn_example: 他患有神经紊乱症。

vocab.definition: a good feeling, reaction, or response
vocab.example: I adopted a positive outlook on life.
vocab.cn_example: 我选择了一种积极的人生观。

vocab.definition: the emotion we feel when we are proud
vocab.example: She has too much pride to accept any help.
vocab.cn_example: 她自尊心太强，不肯接受任何帮助。

vocab.definition: an attitude of admiration or esteem
vocab.example: I respect him as a doctor.
vocab.cn_example: 我尊敬他这个医生。

vocab.definition: to please yourself or someone else
vocab.example: They have 31 flavours of ice cream - enough to satisfy everyone!
vocab.cn_example: 他们有31种口味的冰激凌——足以让所有人都满意！

vocab.definition: very bad or extreme
vocab.cn_meaning: 非常严重的；剧烈的；惨重的
vocab.example: a severe chest infection/leg injury/toothache
vocab.cn_example: 十分严重的胸腔感染／腿伤／牙痛

vocab.definition: used to add new information to what you have just said
vocab.cn_meaning: （表示意外或与通常预期的相反）居然，竟然
vocab.example: They're not married, actually.
vocab.cn_example: 他们实际上没有结婚。

vocab.definition: there is no one with you
vocab.cn_meaning: 单独（的），独自（的）;孤独的（地），无伴的（地）
vocab.example: Exercising alone can be boring.
vocab.cn_example: 独自一个人锻炼可能会很无聊。

vocab.definition: to start to be seen, to arrive, or to exist in a place, especially suddenly
vocab.example: She will appear in court tomorrow.
vocab.cn_example: 她明天出庭。

vocab.definition: a woman who serves food and drink at the tables in a restaurant
vocab.example: She took a job as a waitress.
vocab.cn_example: 她找了个工作，当服务员。

vocab.definition: used to say that something may happen or may be true but you are not certain
vocab.example: Maybe he intends to leave her.
vocab.cn_example: 也许他打算离开她。

vocab.definition: the emotion we feel when we think something is unfair or wrong
vocab.example: I think he feels a lot of anger towards his father, who treated him very badly as a child.
vocab.cn_example: 我想，他对父亲耿耿于怀，是因为小时候受到了他的虐待。

vocab.definition: the emotion we feel when we are extremely worried or stressed
vocab.example: He has helped patients suffering from anxiety, depression, and eating disorders.
vocab.cn_example: 他曾医治过患有焦虑症、抑郁症和进食障碍的病人。

vocab.definition: suffering from anxiety
vocab.example: My mother always gets a bit anxious if we don't arrive when we say we will.
vocab.cn_example: 如果我们没有在说好的时间到达，我母亲总会有些担心。

vocab.definition: to seem attractive or tempting
vocab.cn_meaning: 对…有吸引力;对…有感染力;引起兴趣
vocab.example: It's a programme designed to appeal mainly to 16 to 25-year-olds.
vocab.cn_example: 这个节目的目标观众主要是16到25岁的年轻人。

vocab.definition: to be grateful for something or understand the reason for it
vocab.example: There's no point buying him expensive wines - he doesn't appreciate them.
vocab.cn_example: 给他买名贵的酒没有用——他不懂品酒。

vocab.definition: knowing something has happened or may happen
vocab.cn_meaning: 意识到的;明白的;知道的
vocab.example: I wasn't even aware that he was ill.
vocab.cn_example: 我都不知道他生病了。

vocab.definition: describes an uncomfortable situation, movement, or feeling
vocab.example: It's an awkward corner, so take it slowly.
vocab.cn_example: 这个转弯不好过，开慢点儿。

vocab.definition: the feeling of being relaxed and satisfied
vocab.example: She evidently dresses for comfort.
vocab.cn_example: 显然，她穿着讲究舒适。

vocab.definition: to strongly tell someone to do something
vocab.example: The officer commanded his men to shoot.
vocab.cn_example: 军官命令手下的人射击。

vocab.definition: the feeling of worrying about another person or thing
vocab.example: There's no need for you to concern yourself with what happened.
vocab.cn_example: 你不用操心发生了什么事情。

vocab.definition: the emotion we feel when we believe we can succeed
vocab.cn_meaning: 自信；信心，把握；信赖，信任
vocab.example: I should never have taken him into my confidence.
vocab.cn_example: 我真不该把他当作知心朋友。

vocab.definition: what we feel about a person we admire
vocab.example: There has been a drop in public esteem for teachers.
vocab.cn_example: 公众对教师的尊重程度有所下降。

vocab.definition: far from normal
vocab.example: They live in the extreme south of the island.
vocab.cn_example: 他们住在这个岛的最南端。

vocab.definition: what we feel when we are sudden
vocab.cn_meaning: （尤指突然产生的）恐惧，惊吓;使人惊吓的经历
vocab.example: Our dog took fright at the noise of the fireworks and ran indoors.
vocab.cn_example: 我们的狗听到爆竹声吓得跑进屋来。

vocab.definition: a sad feeling or process we go through, usually when someone we love dies
vocab.cn_meaning: （尤指某人之死引起的）悲痛，悲伤，悲哀
vocab.example: Her grief at her son's death was terrible.
vocab.cn_example: 丧子之痛使她肝肠寸断。

vocab.definition: describes a person or action that has no chance of succeeding
vocab.example: I'm hopeless at sports.
vocab.cn_example: 我在体育方面糟透了。

vocab.definition: describes a person or action that is practical
vocab.example: a sensible answer/approach/compromise/option
vocab.cn_example: 明智的回答／方法／妥协／选择

vocab.definition: describes a feeling of nervousness
vocab.example: There were some tense moments in the second half of the game.
vocab.cn_example: 比赛的下半场有几次紧张的局面。

vocab.definition: thinking of others’ needs and wants
vocab.example: Thank you for calling when I was ill - it was very thoughtful of you.
vocab.cn_example: 我生病时谢谢你打电话来问候——你真是体贴人。

vocab.definition: a large amount of knowledge gained over a long period
vocab.example: I certainly hope to gain a little wisdom as I grow older.
vocab.cn_example: 我当然希望自己随着年龄的增长而多一些智慧。

vocab.definition: to feel a particular emotion, pain etc.
vocab.example: It was a cathartic experience.
vocab.cn_example: 那是一次情感宣泄的体验。

vocab.definition: to succeed in dealing with a difficult problem or situation
vocab.example: I was left to cope on my own.
vocab.cn_example: 就剩下我一个人来单独对付。

vocab.definition: happening regularly or all the time
vocab.cn_meaning: 经常发生的;连续发生的;连续不断的
vocab.example: This entrance is in constant use.
vocab.cn_example: 此入口经常使用。

vocab.definition: having a wound or damage to part of your body
vocab.example: Thankfully, she was not injured.
vocab.cn_example: 万幸的是她没受伤。

vocab.definition: a feeling that you have no hope at all
vocab.example: My handwriting was the despair of my teachers.
vocab.cn_example: 我的字写得很差，使老师们感到十分失望。
